That's because they're using T-mobile & Sprint's networks. Google Fiber was built from the ground up. Google can't just add spectrum to start their own cell network.

The point of GoogleFi (or Ting) is that you only pay for what you use. Do you actually use all 10GB of data per month? Usage-based billing only compares favorably when you compare actual usage. People who use precisely 9.8-9.9 GB each and every month when they pay Verizon for 10 GB will get a better deal with Verizon. The other 98% of people end up wildly overpaying because 2 months out of their 24 month contract they'll use up to that amount of data, when most months they need half or less of what they pay for. In fact, Verizon can offer better looking deals because they can count on that 98% paying more than they need to most of the time.
